title: Section 124 — Voluntarily causing grievous hurt by use of acid, etc.

content.overview: BNS s. 124 — Voluntarily causing grievous hurt by use of acid, etc.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Voluntarily causing grievous hurt by use of acid, and the attempt. Fine is just and reasonable to meet medical expenses of treatment of the victim, and is paid to the victim. Laxmi’s directions sit behind the text.
In student language: BNS s. 124 is the rule on “Voluntarily causing grievous hurt by use of acid, etc”. The section provides that (1) Whoever causes permanent or partial damage or deformity to, or burns or maims or disfigures or disables, any part or parts of the body of a person or causes grievous hurt by throwing acid on or by administering acid to that person, or by using any other means with the intention of causing or with the knowledge that he is likely to cause such injury or hurt or causes a person to be in a permanent vegetative state shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than ten years but which may extend to imprisonment for life, and with fine. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 124 exists so that “Voluntarily causing grievous hurt by use of acid, etc” has a closed legal test in Chapter VI — Of Offences Affecting the Human Body. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Homicide, organised crime, terrorism, hurt, acid, restraint, assault, kidnapping and trafficking.

The provision in detail
124. (1) Whoever causes permanent or partial damage or deformity to, or burns or maims or disfigures or disables, any part or parts of the body of a person or causes grievous hurt by throwing acid on or by administering acid to that person, or by using any other means with the intention of causing or with the knowledge that he is likely to cause such injury or hurt or causes a person to be in a permanent vegetative state shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than ten years but which may extend to imprisonment for life, and with fine:

(2) Whoever throws or attempts to throw acid on any person or attempts to administer acid to any person, or attempts to use any other means, with the intention of causing permanent or partial damage or deformity or burns or maiming or disfigurement or disability or grievous hurt to that person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than five years but which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine

Essential ingredients
1. (1) Whoever causes permanent or partial damage or deformity to, or burns or maims or disfigures or disables, any part or parts of the body of a person or causes grievous hurt by throwing acid on or by administering acid to that person, or by using any other means with the intention of causing or with the knowledge that he is likely to cause such injury or hurt or causes a person to be in a permanent vegetative state shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than ten years but which may extend to imprisonment for life, and with fine:
2. (2) Whoever throws or attempts to throw acid on any person or attempts to administer acid to any person, or attempts to use any other means, with the intention of causing permanent or partial damage or deformity or burns or maiming or disfigurement or disability or grievous hurt to that person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than five years but which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine

Punishment / legal consequence
10 years to life + fine paid to the victim.

Explanations
Explanation 1.—For the purposes of this section, “acid” includes any substance which has acidic or corrosive character or burning nature, that is capable of causing bodily injury leading to scars or disfigurement or temporary or permanent disability

Explanation 2.—For the purposes of this section, permanent or partial damage or deformity or permanent vegetative state shall not be required to be irreversible

Exceptions, limitations and provisos
Provided that such fine shall be just and reasonable to meet the medical expenses of the treatment of the victim:

Provided further that any fine imposed under this sub-section shall be paid to the victim

enhancement.definition: BNS s. 124 consolidates the specialized penal regime against acid attacks: sub-section (1) punishes voluntarily causing permanent or partial damage, deformity, burns, maiming, disfigurement, disability, grievous hurt, or permanent vegetative state by throwing or administering acid with imprisonment of not less than ten years extending to imprisonment for life, and fine; sub-section (2) punishes throwing or attempting to throw or administer acid with imprisonment not less than five years extending to seven years, and fine; fines must be just and reasonable to cover medical treatment and paid directly to the victim.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Imposes severe mandatory minimum sentences against acid attacks and attempted acid throwing while guaranteeing victim compensation to cover specialized reconstructive medical treatment.
statutoryFramework: Chapter VI — Of Offences Affecting the Human Body, BNS s. 124 (consolidating IPC ss. 326A and 326B).

Sub-section (1): Completed acid attack — causing damage, deformity, burns, disfigurement, disability, or persistent vegetative state; punishment: not less than ten years up to imprisonment for life, and fine.
Sub-section (2): Attempted acid attack — throwing or attempting to throw/administer acid; punishment: not less than five years up to seven years, and fine.
Explanation 1: Broad definition of 'acid' including any substance with acidic, corrosive, or burning character capable of causing scars, disfigurement, or disability.
Explanation 2: Explicitly clarifies that damage, deformity, or persistent vegetative state is NOT required to be irreversible.
Proviso: Mandates that any fine imposed shall be just and reasonable to meet medical expenses of treatment, and shall be paid directly to the victim.
essentialIngredients: For sub-section (1): The accused threw acid on or administered acid to the victim, or used other means.
The act caused permanent or partial damage, deformity, burns, maiming, disfigurement, disability, or persistent vegetative state.
The accused acted with the intention of causing, or knowledge that he was likely to cause, such injury or hurt.
For sub-section (2): The accused threw or attempted to throw acid, or attempted to administer acid, with the requisite intent.
For both: The fine imposed must be paid directly to the victim for medical rehabilitation.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 124 consolidates former IPC 326A and 326B. Acid violence is an egregious gender-based and bodily crime that permanently mutilates victims, causing catastrophic physical and psychological trauma. Section 124 establishes two non-bailable sentencing tiers with mandatory minimum terms. Under sub-section (1), any person who causes permanent or partial damage, deformity, burns, disfigurement, disability, or causes the victim to be in a permanent vegetative state faces a mandatory minimum sentence of ten years, extendable to life imprisonment. Explanation 1 adopts a comprehensive scientific definition of 'acid', covering any chemical substance having acidic, corrosive, or burning properties. Explanation 2 codifies a vital legal standard: the prosecution does NOT need to prove that the damage is medically irreversible (eliminating defenses based on reconstructive plastic surgery). Under sub-section (2), the mere attempt to throw or administer acid attracts a mandatory minimum of five to seven years imprisonment. The statutory provisos mandate that the fine must be realistic, cover medical expenses, and be paid directly to the victim.
examples: Teaching example (Sub-section 1 - Facial acid throwing): An accused throws concentrated sulfuric acid into a woman's face after she rejects a marriage proposal, causing third-degree burns, loss of vision in one eye, and severe facial scarring. The accused faces a mandatory minimum sentence of ten years up to life imprisonment under s. 124(1), plus a substantial fine payable to the victim.

Teaching example (Sub-section 2 - Attempted acid throwing): An accused approaches a woman carrying an open container of hydrochloric acid and swings it toward her face; she ducks and the acid splashes harmlessly against a wall. The accused is liable under s. 124(2), facing a mandatory minimum of five to seven years.
distinctions: Section 124(1) vs Section 124(2): Sub-section (1) applies when acid causes injury or damage (minimum 10 years to life); Sub-section (2) applies to the attempt to throw or administer acid (minimum 5 to 7 years).
Section 124 vs Section 118(2): Section 118(2) covers dangerous weapons generally; Section 124 is a specialized acid attack statute with higher mandatory minimums and victim compensation provisos.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether an accused who threw nitric acid on a victim can argue that plastic surgery repaired the damage, meaning no 'irreversible' disfigurement occurred.
Rule: Under Explanation 2 to BNS s. 124, permanent or partial damage or deformity is not required to be irreversible.
Application: The chemical caused corrosive burns and scarring; subsequent surgical intervention does not negate liability under s. 124(1).
Conclusion: The accused is guilty under BNS s. 124(1) and subject to minimum ten years imprisonment.
